message.content:
# Finding ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx

## Using Integration by Parts (twice)

Let **I** = ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx

**First integration by parts:**
- u = cos(x) → du = -sin(x) dx
- dv = exp(x) dx → v = exp(x)

$$I = \exp(x)\cos(x) + \int \exp(x)\sin(x)\, dx$$

**Second integration by parts** (on ∫ exp(x)sin(x) dx):
- u = sin(x) → du = cos(x) dx
- dv = exp(x) dx → v = exp(x)

$$\int \exp(x)\sin(x)\, dx = \exp(x)\sin(x) - \int \exp(x)\cos(x)\, dx = \exp(x)\sin(x) - I$$

## Combining

$$I = \exp(x)\cos(x) + \exp(x)\sin(x) - I$$

$$2I = \exp(x)\cos(x) + \exp(x)\sin(x)$$

$$I = \frac{\exp(x)\cos(x)}{2} + \frac{\exp(x)\sin(x)}{2} + C$$

## Verification

Differentiating the result:

$$\frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{\exp(x)\cos(x)}{2} + \frac{\exp(x)\sin(x)}{2}\right] = \frac{\exp(x)\cos(x) - \exp(x)\sin(x) + \exp(x)\sin(x) + \exp(x)\cos(x)}{2} = \exp(x)\cos(x) \checkmark$$

<answer>exp(x)*cos(x)/2 + exp(x)*sin(x)/2 + C</answer>

I = exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x) - I

2I = exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x)

= exp(x)*[cos(x) + sin(x) - sin(x) + cos(x)]/2
